utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was Goran's position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what his position was, but nobody stood in his way when he was coming to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So he had the insignia of a 2nd Lieutenant; what type of uniform did he wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A multi-coloured camouflage uniform. Goran never wore the regular soldiers' uniform. It always had to be a special uniform, whether a police uniform or a special army unit uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So you knew this man from before you were in Luka camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, I did not know him from before.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you learn his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, he introduced himself to us whenever he could come to Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why would he come to the camp? What would he do there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Every time when Goran Jelisic would come with Kosta's sister, Monika, they would beat four or five men, just like that. He liked to introduce himself, he would say he was Goran Jelisic, that is what he would say, wave the pistol around and said that he killed himself 97 people and that he was going to kill another 97 people in Luka. That is what he used to say.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that you left Luka camp on 7th June of 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, I am having difficulty following who Kosta is; I probably missed that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I believe you mentioned earlier, would you explain again, when you refer to "Kosta" who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I speak about Kosta, Konstantin Simonovic. At that time he wore a uniform, a police uniform, and he introduced himself. He would say that he was the Commander of the Luka camp at Brcko. That was Kosta.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that you left Luka camp on 7th June of 1992. Can you tell us how were allowed to leave on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 7th June at, roughly speaking, 2 p.m., Mr. Rade Bozic came, a captain. He entered accompanied by Kosta into the hangar. Then they called me out, my first name and my surname. I stood up, and Mr. Rade told me, "come nearer", and I went towards them and then Kosta just said, "Oh, come on, do not be afraid, you are going to row for Yugoslavia again". He meant the sport I was good at, and then we shook our hands and said "Hello" and introduced ourselves and then Kosta said, "Well, Rade, we can go out so you could drink a coffee with Isak so that you can get to know each one other better". And so we went out, drank that coffee. He asked me about my nationality, and so on. Then he said, "Would you like me to help you in any way?" and I said, "Yes, if you can, help me to get out of here." He said, "OK, we will see what we can do." Then after that conversation, I said, "Yes, I would like to return to the hangar if you have nothing against it." He said, "OK, go to the hangar and I will do everything I can to take you out of here because your place is not here". That is what he said.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see Captain Bozic again that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did, maybe some two hours later after that first meeting he came again with the same -- in the same vehicle in which he came the first time round, and Kosta accompanied him this time as well, and Kosta was carrying my identity card and a piece of paper that one could put into a typewriter and then he said, "OK, hurry up, Isak, you are going home". And all the other prisoners stood up and we said "goodbye" and they took me out of the hangar. To tell you the truth, I did not know where they were taking me because they simply told me, "You are going home". Whereabouts, I did not know at that time. They just took me out of the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was it who had this piece of paper and your identity card?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Kosta.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was it who told you that you are going home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rade told me that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then he took you away from Luka camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, in that vehicle they had. We sat in that vehicle and drove towards the centre of the town. He asked me where I lived.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of vehicle was this that he was driving?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was a simple or luxury vehicle like the jeeps that you would use in regular traffic. I think the make was Pajero automatic but it had no plates. It had this rotating lights on the roof. They put that later on because it used to be a civilian vehicle.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did he take you after you left the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my flat near the barracks, as I said. I told him to drive me there so we went there. He told me that they will come with me into my flat, and then he told, "Take all your things and you are going to go out of the town; we will stay for a lengthier period".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you able to take all of your possessions from the flat?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I took one bag, one sports bag, with some personal belongings, clothes, nothing more.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After you left your apartment where were you taken then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He told me then whether I would like to go to Belgrade. I said, "Yes" and then he said, "Your wife and your child are there?" I said, "Yes". So he said: "That is where you will go".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is that where he took you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, later on, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Right. Before he took you to Belgrade, did he take you to meet with anyone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I met someone at Zvornik in a motel on the very bank of the River Drina, I met a gentleman, a very important gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Personally Captain Dragan.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know who this Captain Dragan was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew because I saw him before the war in Bosnia on TV. I saw him on TV and I read in the newspapers about him.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was the leader of some kind of special units, as they called them at that time, a volunteers unit that had been formed in the area of Knin, the Serbian Krajina in Croatia. He was very popular among the Serbs in Croatia and in Bosnia and Herzegovina. So he was the commander of these red berets, as they called them, the Kninja.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you were talking with him, were any of these red berets present with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When Rade and I arrived in front of the motel, there in front of the motel there must have been some 30 or 40 of them at the entrance of the motel in Zvornik, and when we parked the vehicle Captain Dragan went out in plain clothes accompanied by journalists from Politika and a lady.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he give some sort of press conference that you saw?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we said "Hello", as if we knew each other for a number of years, very nicely.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know if that was photographed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not then, but in Belgrade, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did this Captain Dragan explain to you why you had been released from the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he did. He told me briefly that my wife had helped me and a sports friend of mine who used to live (and still lives) in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now after this conversation with Captain Dragan, did you eventually go to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we went directly from Zvornik. We crossed into the Republic of Serbia. Captain Dragan was with us, that journalist and the lady from his fund and then Rade drove us towards Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you crossed from Zvornik, is Zvornik in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zvornik is, a little Zvornik partly is not.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So when you passed from the part of Zvornik in Bosnia-Herzegovina into Serbia, did you have any difficulty in being able to enter Serbia there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because on our Bosnian side there used to be a Serb militia checkpoint. They did not stop us but the Serb policemen did stop us because they had a checkpoint there as well. They knew Captain Dragan. He lowered the car window and then they said: "Oh, Captain Dragan", so they let us go.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you remain in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Two months, roughly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: From Belgrade then did you go out of the area of the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, first of all, to Macedonia, and I spent two months there with my wife and my child, and then into western Europe.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Gasi, prior to the conflict coming to the Brcko area, were you a member of any anti-Serb military or paramilitary organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. No, never.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you a member of any organised anti-Serb resistance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After the beginning of the conflict on 30th April, did you become a member of any of these types of anti-Serb organisations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Gasi, could you tell us again your rank during your military service in the JNA, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was just a simple soldier in the traffic unit. That is how it was called. I was just a regular soldier in the traffic unit; literally it meant the driver.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Would you, please, describe to us the regular JNA uniform in 1991, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A grey olivey green uniform -- that means there was a single colour, no kinds of multi-colour lines or patches over it -- with a cap worn on the head, on the head and with a star. That was the uniform of the JNA, be it the regular army or the reservists.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. Could you describe to us the uniform, the regular uniform, of the JNA in 1992 up to May, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All those uniforms, as long as I was in the town of Brcko, were there, these uniforms with these, the old insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: But could you describe to us the uniform of the JNA in the period of January up to May 1992, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I repeat, regular uniforms of the JNA regular soldiers, not any kind of special unit. This was just in one colour which was the grey olivey green colour with buttons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you see that uniform you just described to us after May 19th in Brcko, May, 19th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up until 7th June when I left the camp Luka, I used to see those uniforms. Most of those uniforms were of such a type.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you describe then the regular uniform of the TO, military personnel working with the TO, of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Identical uniforms, identical colour and the reserve strength of the JNA had the same kind of uniforms and the Territorial Defence of that former, whatever it was called at that time, Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So there is no difference between the uniforms of regular JNA and those working with the TO, is there not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war and after the beginning of the war, that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was there any difference then in the month of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I do not know. I did not see. Yes, if you mean the camouflage uniforms, the camouflage uniforms also began to appear in the town, around the town, in the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What was then the difference between the camouflage uniform of the JNA and the camouflage uniform of the TO in the month of May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The camouflage uniforms existed in the Yugoslav People's Army, for special branches of the Yugoslav People's Army. They are regular uniforms; they were at that time and before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you describe that uniform, that camouflage uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Grey olive green with some lighter patches, and those darker nuances were on them. It depended on a particular branch of service that they belonged to. Those who belonged to recognised units were of a lighter colour. The military police, as far as I know, the old JNA, their uniforms were slightly darker.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was there any difference in camouflage uniforms of the JNA and the TO in that period of time, May 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not that I know of.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Do you know when the army of the Republika Srpska was established?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not know. I did not know. I heard it when I was far, far away already. But at that time there was no army of the Republika Srpska while I was in the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So, no army of the Republka Srpske in May 1992 in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you tell us the distinction between those military personnel working with the infantry and those working with the artillery of the TOs? How could one tell by uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that one cannot distinguish members of the artillery units and the infantry units of the Yugoslav People's Army, in the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did the military personnel of the infantry of the TOs have insignia different to the personnel of the TO? Was there any difference within the TO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when the war broke out in Brcko I guess they did not have enough reserve JNA uniforms, so some wore a civilian trousers, and sneakers and tennis shoes, and wore jackets of the uniform or winged jacket or something. That was the difference. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: How would you describe -- no, let me rephrase this question. How can one recognise a member of the paramilitary group by his uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you mean paramilitary groups, that they called that at that time, the only difference were those small emblems they would have on their arms or on the chest somewhere. That would be the difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So the colour of the uniform was the same as those of the TOs, is that not right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The colour of the uniforms worn by special forces and the TOs and the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So the only difference here are those small insignia on those uniforms; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, if you like one could say that, if you wish.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Now let us proceed to equipment. What were the markings on the equipment of the JNA in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have already described them: grey, olive green uniform and a uniform colour of a uniform that was regular, and if you are talking about camouflage special uniforms, I have told you it varied on the branch of service. There was navy of course and their uniforms were dark blue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I am referring to equipment. We are talking about vehicles and all that kind of thing, so equipment. What were the markings of the equipment of the JNA in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Grey, olive green trucks, all types of motor vehicles; they had their plates, their licence plates. So, I really do not follow you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were there any other markings on those vehicles other than the plates?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there were. For instance, the tanks painted grey, olive green, and they would have the plate, an old one, of the Yugoslav People's Army and then the tank would be sprayed over saying that it belonged to the Serb Radical Party from Bijeljina to Chetniks. That would be the difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was there any change in markings on the JNA equipment in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know there was. They changed it. They used to have the star and now they had JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I am not referring to uniforms but to equipment, to vehicles and all that stuff. Was there any change in equipment in 1992, the JNA equipment in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not as far as I could see in Brcko. It was as it was, as it used to be, except that the insignia, the markings on their caps was slightly different.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I am not referring to the markings on uniforms or caps; I am referring to markings on equipment, tanks, vehicles and all that. Do you understand my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right then. Once again, was there any change in markings on the equipment of the JNA in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, there were no changes on the vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Can you tell us what were the markings on the equipment, not uniforms, equipment of the TO in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you mean the Territorial Defence, whether they had tanks or APCs, the Territorial Defence never had them prior to these events.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I am referring to equipment such as, for example, a vehicle. Could you tell us the markings on the vehicles of the TO in 1991, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see that they had changed the colour. Some removed plates, older Yugoslav plates, markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Is that in 1991 or are you referring to a different time frame?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am referring to 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I see. Once again, what were the markings on the TO vehicles in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They did not exist the Territorial Defence did not have any vehicles at that time. They used to borrow them from enterprises. They were civilian vehicles.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. Then we go to 1992. Did the TO have vehicles, military vehicles in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What were the markings on those vehicles in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I told you they removed some markings, some plates from vehicles and some did not. We all saw that in the town. I saw it. So they were old markings.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: From what? Markings from the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, JNA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So what you tell us is that the markings of the JNA were removed and then they got different markings of the TO in 1992; is that what you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am trying to tell you that they took them off some vehicles, and old markings remained on other vehicles ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- while I was in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So, is it true then that in May 1992 one could see in Brcko vehicles with markings of the JNA though working with the TO and vehicles with markings of the TO working with the TO; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Specifically I came across JNA vehicles when I would leave the company, and to my company came also civilian vehicles, mostly civilian vehicles, with the markings written on the paper "TO", and if that is the Territorial Defence, then that is the Territorial Defence, as you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: But how can one tell then if you see a vehicle with, for example, JNA markings on it whether it is in use by the JNA or used by the TO? How can one tell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Specifically, they would have in the front glass. They would have their vehicle. There used to be a paper perhaps of this size with the seal of the JNA garrison in Brcko, and the licence and the permit that it could move around the combat zone.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. Let us move then to the elections of 1990. Do you remember the 1990 elections in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The elections of 1992? The referendum of 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, I am referring to the 1990 elections. Were there elections in 1990?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but you said '92. Yes, all right, 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Very well. You do remember the 1990 elections in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Who won those elections?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I said already the former communists, SDP.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: And the 1992 elections, you remember them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Referendum, not elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. So let us go back to 1990 again, 1990, right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What was the percentage of the SDA in those elections? How many votes? What was the percentage of the votes that the SDA got in these elections?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Perhaps 28 per cent of the total.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What would you say would have been the percentage of the SDS in the 1990 elections?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Approximately 17 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So the SDS won those elections, did not they, if they got 70 or was it 17?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Seventeen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That sounds much more realistic, I would say. What was the percentage then of HDZ in the 1990 elections?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Roughly, I could be wrong by one or two, 22 to 23 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: What was the percentage then of the Former Communists?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They won all the rest that remained up to 100 per cent, so they were the first political party in the local parliament. There were some smaller political parties winning perhaps 1 or 2 per cent. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: The Former Communists were they composed by Muslims, Serbs and Croats, or was there a special large amount of Muslims or a large amount of Serbs in that party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In my town it was made of the members of all three peoples.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Could you tell us about the percentage of the three Major ethnic groups in the Former Communist party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I would not know. I really do not know, but I know they had their list of a mixed composition.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Gasi, you said that you saw no evidence of weapons or arms in the Muslim villages, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Have you told us the truth about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Not a single weapon anywhere?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you have a weapon yourself in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. Legally I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So you had a weapon. In what capacity did you have it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: In what capacity did you have that weapon in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A small pistol.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: How come you had a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A gentleman who arrested me in my company, he was the President of the Shooting Sports Club and when I was proclaimed the sportsman, the athlete of the town in '87 and '89 he handed it to me, that was a gift of a sports club to a sportsman. That was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So you had a weapon in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you have a weapon too in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did until they came and took it away.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: In 1991 did you know anyone who had a weapon who was of Muslim descent?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew hunters. I knew hunters. They had rifles, hunting rifles.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Besides those ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew a number of people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Besides those who were hunting, having hunting rifles, did you know anyone else of Muslim descent having a weapon in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I did. I knew them. My father, he also had a pistol, a trophy pistol of World War II, and brother he also had a pistol but he had a licence for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Your father had a licence, did you say that, or did your brother have a licence for that pistol?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, you heard it well, both had licences, proper licences issued by the authorities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you know other people of Muslim descent having weapons in 1991 except for hunters?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I knew probably those policemen who worked, they had lawful weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: And other people not working with the police in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really do not know about others.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you know anyone of Muslim descent not working with the police, nor being a hunter, having a weapon in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I did not meet such people. Perhaps I did not move in that kind of company among the criminals. Criminals might have had them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Gasi, why did you become a member of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because I wanted to be a member. It was of my own volition.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Was there any special purpose to do that other than a political purpose? Would it provide you with safety or something like that or any other reason?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time, no ----

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you have any ----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: --- it did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Did you have any position in that party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was a member of the Executive Town Committee of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So, I take it that you attended meetings of the SDA, did you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, some of them, yes, in the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: And I suppose you did not only attend public meetings but also closed sessions, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Closed sessions? There were no closed sessions at the time. Gentlemen came from other parties. They were invited. They invited us, other parties invited us and we invited them. I do not know about other closed meetings. I did not take part in any closed sessions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So let us go then to 1991. Did you attend any meeting of the SDA in 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not any more as a member in my capacity of the Executive Committee, but as an observer, as a passerby, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So you did attend meetings of the SDA just as a member, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, no doubt.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were those meetings always in public, that is free access for others than members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not only all members, but all those who wanted to attend that kind of meetings.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: There were discussions at those meetings about weapons, were there not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know nothing about that at those rallies which I attended. Those were election rallies and they did not mention any weapons. I do not know, not really. Not at those rallies. Perhaps at some others, but I do not know. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Mr. Gasi, you were a member of the Kayak Klub, Haris Suljic, were you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Right. Were there also Serb members of that club?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were good friends.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis? Re-Examination.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Gasi, concerning weapons possessed either by Serbs or Muslims, you had indicated earlier that when you were doing your duties out in villages you began to see on occasions that JNA weapons were distributed to Serb civilians. Did you ever in your travels to the Muslim villages see these types of JNA weapons distributed to Muslim civilians?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I moved about a great deal around all the villages in the Brcko municipality, and believe me, I never, really never, saw JNA members distributing weapons to Muslims. This was the exclusive right they gave to the Serbs. I know nothing else.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: You had also mentioned earlier that you saw in Serb villages, you began to see heavy weapons such as artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I would object to that question, your Honour. I think it is not within the cross-examination these questions.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I be heard?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The Defence has raised the issue of arming the Muslims. I am simply clarifying this with my witness on redirect.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think you are now moving into artillery and heavy equipment. The Defence on cross-examination asked the witness whether he could tell the difference between JNA artillery and weapons, no, equipment, vehicles I should say, and TO. When I say "TO", Territorial Defence, TO. I gather this is what you are now moving into, is that not so?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: My understanding of the questioning, and perhaps I had it wrong, was that the questioning from the Defence had to do in general with the arming of the Muslims. I do not believe the questioning specifically limited whether they were receiving automatic weapons or whether they were receiving larger type weapons. Perhaps I have misunderstood the cross-examination, but that is my understanding of it. Therefore, I also wanted to ----

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The question that you objected to, Mr. Wladimiroff, was whether or not the witness had seen heavy vehicles and artillery. Is that not your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: That is right, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: The basis of it is that it goes beyond the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Now, in response to that, what do you say, Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am simply saying my understanding of the way the Defence worded their cross-examination had to do in general with arming of Muslims, and to the extent that implied larger weapons than hand-held weapons I would like to cover that. If they were speaking only of arming the Muslims with hand-held weapons, then I will not cover the artillery.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I did not deal with that subject. I dealt with the identification of uniforms and equipment, and I dealt with knowledge about weapons with Muslims. I did not deal with any weapons that were with Muslims with Serbs whatsoever, and I did not deal with the giving of weapons to Muslims either. So I think it is beyond the cross-examination, this question.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: My colleagues say it is beyond cross-examination. Actually, I thought you were going into another area. I thought you were asking this witness whether or not he had seen any heavy equipment and artillery. That was objected to. I do not see that that is beyond cross-examination, but I will defer to my two colleagues. I thought the next question was going to be: Could he distinguish between JNA heavy artillery and TO heavy artillery, which was certainly within the cross-examination. But I will sustain the objection.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Following up on the Judge's understanding of my question, I would like to ask you a question concerning whether you ever observed the TO with any type of artillery weapons, TO in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know before the war how the Territorial Defence was armed. I can speak about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: And what were the arms of the Territorial Defence before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those weapons were in companies, so light infantry weapons, no tanks, no guns, no helicopters or armoured vehicles. That did not exist in the Territorial Defence before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: So the types of weapons the Territorial Defence had were what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Light infantry weapons, automatic rifles, semi-automatic rifles, those old JNA rifles and 48. Those were the weapons that were in the company where I worked in Elektrodistribucija. That is what I know about the TO.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: I have nothing else to question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I have one question. You mentioned that in 1992 the insignia on the cap or hat of the JNA was changed from a star to the initials "JNA". Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. Those were symbols that were written in Cyrillic alphabet.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: And would that change also apply to the TO which I think you sometimes call the Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When they changed those insignia, I cannot remember anything changed in the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Does that then mean that the Territorial Defence continued to wear the star that previously the JNA had been wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, because they had old uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: When did this change from a star to Cyrillic JNA take place in 1992, what month?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The change in my town which I saw then, but that happened slightly earlier; I could even say at the end or maybe in mid-1991 when those events happened in Slovenia and Croatia. I cannot remember the exact date but the instructions were given for that to be changed. We could hear about it on the radio and see it on the TV.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Just a couple of questions, Mr. Gasi. How far is Brcko from the Prijedor Opstina, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Roughly speaking, I can tell you that. To Banja Luka I think it is something 180 kilometres and then from Banja Luka to Prijedor 210; 210 kilometres I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: Were you released from the Luka camp on June 7th 1992 or July 7th 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was 7th June 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Miss Hollis, do you have additional questioning?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to Mr. Gasi being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine. You may be excused permanently. Thank you, Mr. Gasi. We will stand in recess for lunch until 2.30. (1.00 p.m.)

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, would you call your next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Your Honour, we would call Mr. Redzic. MR. FADIL REDZIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you take the oath, please, Mr. Redzic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, would you please state your full name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Fadil Redzic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born on 4th August 1946.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am a Muslim, a Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your place of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you live in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born there in 1946 and I stayed there up until the war broke out in 1992. I did not go anywhere else.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say were you born and lived in Brcko, do you mean the town of Brcko in the Opstina of Brcko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The town of Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was your prior occupation, Mr. Redzic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a mechanical technician.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did you work?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the textile plant, Interplet, at Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you work there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 23 years.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever perform any active duty, military service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did you perform this active duty service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In 1966 when I was in the school for Reserve officers at Zadar.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where is that school located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Zadar, in the Republic of Croatia. It is in the middle of the Adriatic coast.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you study there in your course for Reserve officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was trained there to become an officer of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have any area of speciality within the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My speciality in the Reserve officers corps was the training on the gun B76 millimetre. That was an artillery gun.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that you trained as a Reserve officer. Can you tell us within the JNA structure what was the difference between the Reserve component and the active duty component?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We had military service for a year for the people who were in the Reserve officers school; whereas the others that had the regular, that were the regulars conscripts spent some 15 or 16 months and the active duty officers went to the Military Academy and after that they became part of the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As Reserve officer then, you did not have full-time employment as a JNA officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Concerning this artillery training that you received, you said that this lasted a period of six months. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, six months.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After you completed that training, what rank were you given?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a Sergeant.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you received the six months of training, your instructors, to your knowledge, were these active JNA officers or were they Reserve officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were all active duty JNA officers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were these officers of mixed nationality or were they Serbs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of them were Serbs, but it was mixed.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Upon graduation where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to Delnice for training.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In what Republic is that located in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Delnice is in the Republic of Croatia in the northern part of the coast.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you receive training at Delnice?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed there for six months.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of training did you receive there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was a Commander of a gun 76 mixed artillery, anti-aircraft.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What size unit did you command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Delnice, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, at Delnice.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the second battery with some 60 or 70 people; it depends really on the type of the unit.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you in command of the battery or of a smaller division of the battery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was the battery.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: All right. You said that you were a Commander there. What type of unit did you command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: An artillery unit.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many weapons did you have under your command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The battery had six weapons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You yourself commanded how many?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The whole battery of six weapons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After your six months of training and working as a Commander at Delnice, what rank did you achieve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I became a 2nd Lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did you go after this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went back to Brcko, my home town.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Once you returned to Brcko did you continue in the JNA reserves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did. I continued with my work as a Reserve officer in the 395th Brigade Veljko Lukic Kurjak.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you continue in the JNA reserves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Up until 31st of December 1991.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that you were assigned to the 395th Brigade; tell us again where that Brigade was located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The 395th Brigade was located at Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the name of the military barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The barracks were called Veljko Lukic Kurjak.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In what part of Brcko were those barracks in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Almost in the very centre of the town.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was this brigade part of the active duty JNA or was it a Reserve brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Part -- it was part of an active duty unit.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was its combat status -- combat ready or Reserve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It had combat ready, war A1 type of status.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of units were assigned to this Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That Brigade was mixed; there were various types of units in it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were the types of units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It had an armoured battalion, a motorized Battalion and artillery division, light anti-armoured tank division, then some rare type of signalling unit and all kinds of other types of services that formed that particular Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To what division was this Brigade assigned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In fact, the division belonged to the 395th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The 395th Brigade belonged to what organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the Army -- I cannot quite understand what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry. The Brigade, what was the next higher echelon from the Brigade in terms of chain of command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Division.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was that located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That Division was located at Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was this an active duty or Reserve Division at Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: War, that means combat A unit.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you returned to Brcko, what was your position in the 395th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the 395th Brigade, I was assigned to the mixed anti-armoured unit and I was the Commander of the second gun battery.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of weapons did you have command over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was commanded anti-armoured types of weapons. The type of gun is called ZIS 416.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The ZIS is primarily used for what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is anti-tank exclusively, but it can be used for other things.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the following years, until the end of 1991, what positions did you hold with the 395th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the 395th Brigade, apart from being the Commander of the second gun battery, I was also the Deputy Commander of that mixed artillery battery. After that, I became the head in charge of the battery.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During this time that you were in the 395th Brigade, where did you perform your duties, at the military barracks or at other locations as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at the military barracks but elsewhere as well.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In what other locations would you perform these duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We used to go to various types of training exercises; it depends where.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So the unit would actually deploy to another location for a training exercise?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As a Reserve officer, how much time did you devote to your military duties each year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Each year, on an average, between one month to one month and a half.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During this time you were with the 395th Brigade, during this one to one and a half month period, what types of duties would you perform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, these things I told you; the head of the artillery, if I was in the Brigade or, in a smaller unit, I was the Deputy Commander of a smaller artillery unit.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you became the Deputy Commander and later you became the head of the artillery division, what types of duties would you be involved with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As the head of the artillery, I co-ordinated the work of the mixed anti-armoured smaller division or the howitzer.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you ever involved in any co-ordination involving training for the rest of the Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I only worked on the artillery type of duties.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you involved in any types of training regarding artillery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were mostly preparing for performing the duties of the training exercise and, after that, we would go and perform that particular duty like shooting with real ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you received new weapons, did you participate in any type of training regarding these new weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Whatever weapons arrived to the 395th Brigade, no matter it was artillery or something else, we had to become familiar with, to familiarise with that type of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At the end of 1991, did the Territorial Defence exist in the Brcko area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They did.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you know, who was the Commander of the Territorial Defence forces?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Commander of the Territorial Defence of Brcko was Lieutenant Colonel Milisav Milutinovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met him through the whole work I did, through my Reserve duties, but he was otherwise a teacher of history.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did the Territorial Defence have weapons available to it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Territorial Defence did have weapons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Various kinds of weapons; it depends on the particular composition of the Territorial Defence unit. If they had equipment, infantry, weapons, automatic, semi-automatic weapons and grenade launches, mortar launches.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were these weapons kept?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These weapons were exclusively stored in warehouses.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time you were still a Reserve officer in the Brigade, did you become aware of these weapons being taken from the TO by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, all the Territorial Defence weapons that were in companies were taken out of those companies and partly put in the hangars at Teslic and partly in the JNA barracks.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You say in the hangars at Teslic, what is this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, it was Krepsic. That was a warehouse of equipment, of the whole equipment, on the 395th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That included weapons as well as other equipment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. All weapons and equipment of the Brigade were there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you ever present at your own workplace when the JNA came and took weapons, took TO weapons, from your workplace?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was personally present when the army took the weapons from my textile plant, Interplet, and it was taken away on a military truck.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Which time frame was this that these weapons were taken away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was in the course of the year 1991.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that at least some of these weapons were taken to the barracks in Brcko. How did you become aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I learned that while I was still in the Reserve. All the hangars that were there were part of the equipment was and part of the equipment was taken away earlier, and I was -- I later heard on from the officers that were there that it was taken from the TO, and I personally saw the weapons as well.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You heard from JNA officers there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I was also at the barracks at that time.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During 1991 did you become aware of any -----

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, while I was in Reserves in September up until 31st December.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This was the time period during which these TO weapons were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but before they took all these weapons from the companies.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So, prior to September they had taken the weapons from the companies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During 1991, did you become aware of any distribution of weapons by the JNA to inhabitants of the Brcko area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During 1991, those weapons, while I was in Reserve, from the month of September 1991 up until 31st December, that those weapons were distributed exclusively to the inhabitants of the Serb nationality.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you become aware of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time I was in the Reserve.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did that enable you to know that this redistribution was occurring?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was personally present because I was there on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As of 31st December 1991, do you have any idea how many personnel were assigned to the 395th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The exact number, I cannot say how many people received arms, but the complete weaponry of the 395th Brigade was distributed the members of the Serb nationality.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry, let me repeat my question: By the end of 1991, how many personnel were assigned to the 395th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, in the 395th Brigade there were 3,300 people. That was the number of the people, that personnel, in the Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These personnel were comprised of whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only the people that belonged to the Serb nationality.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were these individuals both active duty and Reserve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty and Reserve officers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In December 1991, when you left the Brigade, what type of weaponry did the Brigade have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Brigade had, as I said previously, APCs, artillery division, mixed anti-armoured artillery division, howitzer, 103 millimetres, then signalling AB headquarters, and all the other accompanying services as I mentioned before.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The artillery division, how many weapons did it have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The artillery division had 12 guns, anti-tank, 76 millimetres, and howitzer division had also 12 howitzers of 122 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did the Brigade possess any anti-aircraft artillery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It had light PVO anti-aircraft division, 133 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The motorised divisions would have had what type of weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The motorised battalion had 60, 80 and 120 grenades, grenade -- mortar launches, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At the time that you left the Brigade, the Brigade also have anti-tank rockets that were on a mounted chassis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It had APCs with guided missiles, AP11.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was in command of these APCs with guided missiles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Commander of the APCs with guided missiles was Stefan Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was that unit located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The unit was located in Djakovo in the Republic of Croatia, and later on it was transferred to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was it transferred to in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was transferred in the village of Pelagicevo, some 15 to 18 kilometres away from Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did that transfer occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It occurred in October. I saw that in October 1991.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know Lieutenant Colonel Nikolic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew him then when I met him in 1991 -- only then.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was he an active duty or a Reserve officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He as an active duty officer of the JNA. He was a Lieutenant Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you learn where he was from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Through this whole story because we co-operated for the transfer of the weapons from Djakovo to Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you learn where he originally was from, where his home was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only know that he is a Serb. I do not know where he comes from exactly.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever learn why this unit moved from Djakovo to Pelagicevo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I never learned that, no.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These weapons that you have talked about that were in the possession of the 395th Brigade, for example, the 122 millimetre howitzers, what is the range of such a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The range is 21 kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The ZIS canon, what is the range of such a weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ZIS, 17 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The antiaircraft artillery, can that be used for any purpose other than as an anti-aircraft weapon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it can.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If it is used for another purpose, what would be its range?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The range of the aircraft artillery would be 800 to 1,000 metres.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, when you left the Brigade in December 1991, other than the JNA, did any other groups in the area have 122 millimetres howitzers or ZIS canon?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Brigade had only that kind of canons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did any other group to your knowledge have anti-aircraft artillery?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, just the artillery brigade, 395th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did any other group have armoured personnel carriers or tanks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that the 395th Brigade was located in the military barracks in the centre of Brcko. Was most of the weaponry located there as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of the weaponry was located in the village of Krepsic not far from Brcko. All the weapons and equipment of the Brigade were there. Part of the weaponry was only stored in the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, in 1991 were weapons moved from Krepsic to other locations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the course of 1991, most of the armaments from Krepsic and other equipment and material was transferred to neighbouring villages, Donja and Gornja - Bukovica, Razljeva, Pipara, and some of it was transferred to the village of Pelagicevo.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These other villages to which these weaponry were transferred, to your knowledge, what was the ethnic composition of these villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ethnic composition was Serb, exclusively.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: By the end of 1991, had units of the Brigade moved from the military barracks to other locations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The complete Brigade was taken out of the barracks and transferred to those places I just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did any units at all remain at the military barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did any personnel remain at the military barracks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, some personnel remained in the barracks. The Commander, Pavle Milenkovic, was there and Deputy Commander for political work, Lieutenant Colonel Slavko Debic, Captain Petrovic and other personnel of the Brigade, that is, lower ranking officers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Why did you leave the 395th Brigade in December 1991?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: During the drill, Muslim officers were ignored so that I decided to leave the Yugoslav People's Army on 31st December 1991.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What do you mean that other officers were "ignored"?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, they did not invite us to meetings, and whenever they had to hold some important meeting they would let us go home.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did this exclusion begin?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, sometime in November or December it was.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have mentioned some of the persons in command positions at the 395th Brigade. I would like to speak with you for a moment about that. You indicated that Pavle Milenkovic was the Commander of the Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was the Commander of the 395th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his rank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was Lieutenant Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was he an active duty or a Reserve officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was active duty officer.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know what his ethnic group was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where his home was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He lived in Brcko but, as far as I know, his home was in Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where is Novi Sad located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he have a Deputy Commander at the Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Deputy Commander for political activity was Slavko Debic and the Chief of the Staff was Slobodan Milinkovic from Nis.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Slavko Debic, was he an active duty or a Reserve officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty; Lieutenant Colonel.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Croat.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Major Milinkovic, what his status? Was he active duty or a Reserve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where his home was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He lived in Brcko but his home was in Nis.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where is Nis located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You also mentioned a Captain Petrovic; what was his position in the Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was Deputy Commander for intelligence matters.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was he active duty or a Reserve?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active duty.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where he was from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The next level of command below that would have consisted of what positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next level below that, below the Brigade? Could you please repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes. You have named the Brigade Commander and his deputies. The next level of command below them would have consisted of what positions?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was Deputy Commander for political affairs, head for intelligence matters, Deputy Commander for logistics and all other branches of service, that is, head of artillery, of anti-aircraft, defence engineer, head of engineering division -- of engineering section, etc. That would be the command of the Brigade, properly speaking.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know all of these gentlemen as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was their status? Were they active duty officers or Reserve officers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them were active duty, some of them were in the Reserve.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you left the Brigade who replaced you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My post was taken by Zoran Pajic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his rank?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a Major at the time.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where he was from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These other persons in positions of authority, do you know their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are all Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you left the Brigade at the end of December 1991, to your knowledge, were you the last Muslim who had held a command position there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know a Lieutenant Hajro Radonjcic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did know; he was a 2nd Lieutenant at the time, Hajro Radonjcic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was he an active duty or Reserve officer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Active officer.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know where his home was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Brcko, but he originally came from Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where is Kosovo located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: From the time you left the Brigade, from 31st December 1991 until 30th April 1992, did you ever see any of these persons who had command positions in the Brigade in Brcko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, we used to met in the town until the conflicts broke out in Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: From 30th April until 8th May 1992, did you ever see any of these individuals personally or see them on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On television, I saw Captain Petrovic and Commander of the 395th Brigade, Lieutenant Colonel Pavle Milenkovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were they doing on the television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The main purpose of their being on television was to say that there would be no war in the town of Brcko and to tell people not to leave. That was the JNA offering security.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In the summer of 1992, do you recall learning about Lieutenant Colonel Milenkovic's reassignment from the 395th Brigade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Lieutenant Colonel Pavle Milenkovic was transferred, reassigned and Lieutenant Colonel Kutlesic, Milorad Kutlesic, took his post.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did you hear this announcement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I learned about it on television and media in the town.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did you hear this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: July.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No -- yes, it was July 1992, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did the announcement indicate where Lieutenant Colonel Milenkovic was being reassigned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no, nothing was said about it, but I saw him on television in person. He was on the days during a ceremony in Novi Sad and television transmitted that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You saw him there after this announcement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In the spring of 1992, did you observe any changes in your ability to get certain radio or television stations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there was local television Brcko and radio Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did there come a time that you were unable to get other channels you had previously been able to receive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, one cannot hear anything afterwards when the bridges were blown up.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What could you receive, what stations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean television or radio?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: First television, what could you receive on television?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could hear Novi Sad, Belgrade, Zagreb, Sarajevo on television.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After the bridges were blown, what could you receive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only Belgrade and Novi Sad.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On the radio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We could hear Sarajevo, Belgrade and those other radio stations.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After the bridges were blown, were you able to receive all of those stations as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we still received only Belgrade and Novi Sad and Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After the bridges were blown up in Brcko on 30th April, did you send your family from the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My family then left for a safe place.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
