utterances.text: Did you remain in the town of Brcko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did you stay?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in my house.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That is located in what area of Brcko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is at Mujkici.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: That section of Brcko was comprised of what ethnic group or groups?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims constituted the majority. Over 95 per cent were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You remained in your home in the Mujkici section of Brcko until what date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I stayed in my flat until 8th May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During this time period from 30th April when the bridges were blown up and 8th May, were there additional attacks on the town of Brcko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, as beginning with 1st May until 8th May, shelling of Brodusa, Dizdarusa, Klanac, Suljagica Sokak, Meraje, Mujkici and then on further.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These names that you have just given are these sections of Brcko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what ethnic group or groups inhabited those sections of Brcko?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims were the majority, over 95 per cent.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Based upon your military training and experience, were you able to recognise what types of weapons were being used to shell those sections?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mortars 60, 80, 120 millimetres and 122 millimetre howitzers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time of the blowing up of the bridge on 30th April and also the time of the shelling that followed, were you aware of any resistance by the local inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Armoured resistance was offered, at the moment was offered in Dizdarusa, Brodusa, Klanac, Mujkici and Suljagica Sokak.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the nature of that resistance, what type of weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I thought, by and large, infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time period of 30th April until 8th June while in the Mujkici section, did you have any conversations with any JNA officers that you know?

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I think you mean 8th May.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on the telephone I talked to an officer and a colleague gave me the number of the barracks, and I asked them to take my family out. The telephone was answered by Milorad Sehovac and said that was out of the question, and that he would burn down that whole area. Those were the words he used.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. A correction for the record; I did mean until 8th May. (To the witness): You said a Major Milorad Sehovac, how did you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, I knew him, he was in the Brigade. He was a Major, active Major, and he headed an infantry battalion.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You had called him to ask him to assist you in getting out of that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his response to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That was out of the question and that he would burn down that area.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On 8th May what happened to you on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 8th May 1992 at 8.30, I was called by the paramilitary of self-appointed Major Mauzer.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who were you with at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I, at that moment, I was with my brother, his wife and their two children, my sister, my brother-in-law and their two children and Ramadam Mujadzic and his wife, Radmila Mujadzic, had come to visit us and we were marking the May Day.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At the time that these personnel of Major Mauzer captured you, were you armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were any of the people you were with armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, none of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These people that captured you at this time, can you describe what kind of uniforms they were wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage uniforms. They had black caps on their heads and they were painted all sorts of colours and they were armed very well indeed.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise the weapons that they had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had automatic rifles, mostly automatic rifles, and there were also a number had grenades, knives at their belts, two knives in their boots, two knives at the back.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Based on your training and experience, did these automatic weapons appear to be JNA military type weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall if they had any type of insignia or patches on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had, whether on the left or right shoulder, I cannot remember exactly, but they had the Serbia flag with four Ss.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Once you and these other individuals were captured, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That day we were taken to the cellar of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you went to the hospital did you see any weapons near the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Near the hospital itself there were the anti-aircraft guns. Some of them belonged to the light anti-armoured, anti-tank division.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise those as the type of weapons the 395th Brigade had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, those weapons belonged to the 395th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see any type of flag or flags being flown?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time on the hospital, I saw the Red Cross flag, the white one with the red cross and the Serbian flag hanging at the entrance of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you went to the hospital were there other people there as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we entered this cellar of the hospital there were many Muslim inhabitants who were captured in Mujkici at the time and were all taken to that cellar.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you also see persons with military uniforms at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I saw many in uniforms, in SMB uniforms, of the former JNA and the paramilitaries of Major Mauzer wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You have mentioned this Major Mauzer; when you were taken to the hospital, did you know that one of the men there, did you know his name was Major Mauzer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that point of time when I was captured, no, I did not know, but when we were in the cellar I heard from his soldiers who talked about him.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This man referred to as Major Mauzer, did you ever see him again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I met this man in Brezovo Polje. We were detained when they took us from there to Brezovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At that time did he tell you his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then how did you learn his name there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I learned his name from his soldiers who were moving about that cellar because there were a number of those soldiers in the cellar, and we were siting in a corner on a bench, and it was then that I learned his true name and surname.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were his soldiers dressed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His soldiers were in camouflage uniforms, so they had black caps and were painted -- they had painted faces and, as I told you, they had two knives behind their back, two knives in their belt and two knives in their boots, and they were also carrying lots of ammunition belts around their own -- over the chest.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see any type of patches or insignia on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw their uniform the same thing that I saw on the first (indecipherable) rather, the Serbian flag and four Ss.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: This man that you were told was Major Mauzer, what has he doing when you saw him at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He had come from Bijeljina and he belonged, I learned that afterwards, that he belonged to the military -- paramilitary group of Black Panthers Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was he doing when you saw him at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, then lined up his soldiers not far from me, some two or three metres away, and he was to continue cleansing the Mujkici and he ordered his men, he ordered them in person, I heard that, that today, no prisoners. As I translated it, it was whoever you capture, you kill him.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you held at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the hospital from 8.30 to about 1500 hours.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you taken from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Around 1500 or 3.30 we were taken to Brezovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How far away from Brcko is Brezovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Brezovo Polje is some 14, 15 kilometres away.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is the ethnic composition of Brezovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a Muslim place exclusively with the exception of a couple of teachers who were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were you taken to Brezovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Buses, they took us in buses.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were they military buses or civilian buses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a civilian bus, but it was driven by a man in a grey, olive green uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you taken there alone or were others taken there with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The whole family, that is, my family, my brothers and sisters, and there were some 15 to 20 persons more.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you held at Brezovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At Brezovo Polje I was detained from 8th May 92 to 1st June, sorry, 17th June 1992, 17th June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were there other persons who were also held there during that same time period?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and there were many detainees from Brcko who had been transferred to Brezovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of these detainees, in addition to your family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, yes, I knew almost all those who came from Brcko because I had lived and worked with them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were all Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were in the Brezovo Polje were you free to leave to Brezovo Polje as you wished?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we could -- no, we were not free to leave Brezovo Polje because it was blocked all around by this, by army.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These individuals you referred to as the "army", what type of uniforms did they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Grey olive green uniforms, most of them. One of them had a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time you were at Brezovo Polje were you physically abused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, several times I was physically abused, harassed, battered.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was done to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Srdjan, Zeljko, Ratko.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They beat me until I lost conscious. They destroyed my right eye.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did they destroy your eye?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While they beat me with sticks, with boxes, with pistols, some 45 to one hour they kept at it, beating me.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You named several individuals as those who beat you. Did you know these individuals prior to being taken to Brezovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not know them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you learn their names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I learned their names because there they held us on those premises, and every morning at 8 o'clock all the able bodied men, we had to report at 8 o'clock in the morning and 5 o'clock in the afternoon. They would single out five or six people from those groups for interrogation. They never said what kind of interrogation, and they used to beat people and I was one of those people who were beaten and they did it every day.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: But how did you become aware of their names? Did they tell you or did someone else tell you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We learned their names from the people who moved around and from the villages, from Brezovo Polje. That is how we learned their real names.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that you had to report to people each day while you were at Brezovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Every morning we had to report at 8 o'clock and then in the afternoon at 5 o'clock, 1700 hours, so that they would have some kind of a registry, so that nobody would leave.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The people who were held there, what was their gender?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly men, and some women, everybody, men and women, but the worst thing was that nobody from that village was able to get out from there, nobody.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What about the age groups, were there only adults or children as well as adults?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were also children there, quite a lot of children.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During this time you were held at Brezovo Polje, do you recall seeing any officers from the 395th Brigade come to Brezovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I can recall that. In that time frame while I was at Brezovo Polje, very near the place where I lived, Slobodan Milinkovic came, Major Slobodan Milinkovic, with the 2nd Lieutenant, Hajro Radonjcic, and then there were other people with grey olive uniform with red berets on their heads. From the top floor of that house they were overlooking at a village, Racinovci, which is across the river in Croatia, across the River Sava.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the times that Major Milinkovic came to Brezovo Polje, did you ever speak with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I never spoke to him. Only at that moment when I saw him, the police came to take me for interrogation, he only said "hello" and that was all.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall the time period that you saw him in the village of Brezovo Polje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know quite well that it was in May 1992. It was in an afternoon, around 4 o'clock in the afternoon, before we were taken for interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have any idea what part of May, what part of the month, when you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think somewhere in mid-May.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You said at the time that he was there some police came to take you for interrogation; did you recognise any of these police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no. I did not recognise any of the policemen.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He wore a police uniform, their police, Serb police uniform.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Civilian police uniform or a military police uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Can you describe that uniform for us, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The uniform was blue with a blue beret and with a Serb flag as insignia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you taken for interrogation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They took us to the school. The name of the school is 25th May.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The people who interrogated you, did you recognise any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I did not, not at that moment.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They wore police uniforms, the blue police uniform with a beret and a Serb flag on the cap.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did beatings occur at these interrogations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not then, because that was the first time they took me for interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So you went subsequently to be interrogated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, at several times I was taken for interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Each time you were taken for interrogation, was it individuals wearing these police uniforms who interrogated you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was taken by the people wearing the grey olive green uniforms, and when we would arrive there we would find people in camouflage uniforms. Srdjan, Zeljko and Ratko were there among the others and also Slobodan Markovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who were those individuals you have just named?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were their paramilitary groups that were there, I do not know for what reasons. They had some duties, I cannot tell you what reasons, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At these subsequent interrogations were you beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you left the village of Brezovo Polje where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 17th June 1992, first of all, all the people from Brcko were put into the gym of the school, the 25th May, and then about an hour later all the men from Brezovo Polje were also imprisoned in the gym of the school, the 25th May, and there we were taken to the notorious camps of Luka Brcko.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you kept there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was at Luka between 17th June up until 1st July 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Luka, did you know any of the guards at the camp there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, when we arrived to Luka, I recognised Kosta Simeunovic by the nickname of Kole who was the Commander of that camp at that time. He is an interior decorator.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of the other camp personnel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean exactly?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Camp guards or other personnel who worked at the camp, did you know any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew several people who were there from Brcko. Among them was Radoje Boric called "Okac" called, then Slobodan Radenkovic and Predrag Dokic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These people you have just named, what positions had they held prior to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rade, who used to be the guard there, he was a driver at my company, textile plant, Interplet, and Predrag Dokic was also a driver there at Interplet. There were quite a few people coming from the SUP to Luka.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Coming to Luka from the SUP, in what capacity, working there or as detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they were inspectors of the Serbian SUP, and mostly every day they would take out people, interrogate them, abuse and beat.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did they take you out while you were at Luka camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of uniforms did they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The people who came from the SUP wore plain clothes, and Kosta Simeunovic, Kole, who at that time was the Commander of the camp wore blue trousers and a police blue blouse.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Luka camp, did any military people come into the camp who did not work there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People came, personally I did not know those people, but mostly they would come in a jeep with a picture of Captain Dragan on that jeep wearing red berets, and wearing a red beret, and down it was written "Captain Dragan".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time that you were at Luka camp, did you know any of the other detainees held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew all the people from Brcko. Most of them were Muslims. There were also some Croats and some Albanians.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After you left Luka camp, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Luka, I started to live with a friend of mine at his place. His name was Asarevic, Hasan.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was that place located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not far from Luka, some 400 or 500 metres from there, so in the immediate neighbourhood of the ex JNA building.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At that time in the town, that is, from 1st July 1992, I stayed in the town until 9th March 1994 when I was exchanged.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After you returned to Brcko, to this area of Brcko, were you required to do any type of duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At several occasions I was taken to the SUP by their policemen for interrogation. They harassed me. I had to dig roads and I had also -- I was also under labour direction. I was also kept in a primary school for nine days and nine nights with other people from Brcko without any food.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How was it that in 1994 you were allowed to leave the Brcko area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was an exchange that took place between Brcko and Tuzla. I was exchanged by the 2nd Corps of the army of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, prior to 30th April 1992, were you a member of any anti-Serb military or paramilitary organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was not.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you a part of any organised anti-Serb resistance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After 30th April until the time that you were captured, were you a member of any such organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We have no questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, this witness and the previous witnesses have referred to what are either SNB uniforms or SMB uniforms; I wonder if you can elucidate that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you. MISS HOLLIS (To the witness): Mr. Redzic, in your testimony you have referred to former JNA uniforms as SMB uniforms; could you tell us what you mean by SMB uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These uniforms were worn by the former JNA. They were grey, olive green colour uniforms, but as at that time there were probably not enough camouflage uniforms they could wear, most of those soldiers, Reserve soldiers, wore the grey, olive green uniforms, SMB. That is where every time I mentioned the word "SMB" this means grey, olive green. They were really -- they really wore those uniforms, and all the others that I described wore the camouflage uniforms. That is how I described them and that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So the SMB uniform was the regular uniform of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. This was the regular, regular JNA uniform, and we wore it all as reservists and all the conscripts wore it while doing their military service.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: I just have one, I think: Did I understand the witness to say that all of the persons in the 395th Brigade were Serbian except, of course, you were in the reserves, is that correct, so are you saying that all of the persons in the 395th Brigade were Serbians, that is, the regular members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You were a member of the Reserves of the 395th Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, but that was up until 31st December 1991, then I left after that date. I answer to your question is the situation after 31st December 1991, then I left the Reserve, the Reserves, and the complete 395th Brigade was Serbian from then on.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, as I understand the testimony, the 395th Brigade, the regulars, were all Serbian, is that correct? Is that your understanding? You may want to put the question to the witness. Of course, he is Muslim, Bosniak, and he was in the Reserves of the 395th Brigade. I am trying to understand if I am correct. I understand when he left that there were no more Muslims, I understand that, but what I want to get clear is that the regulars in the 395th Brigade were Serbs, all Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Redzic, you have indicated that after you left the 395th Brigade on 31st December 1991, then the Brigade was totally Serb; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think that it is correct. All the Muslims left the 395th Brigade and to replace them came only Serbian Reservists, so ethnically it became completely Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So when you say that the 395th Brigade became exclusively Serb, you are speaking of both the active duty component and the Reserve component?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, both.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Fine, thank you. Do you have any additional questions, any cross-examination in the light of that, Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any objection to the witness being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: None whatsoever, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: You may be permanently excused. Thank you very much for coming you are excused.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, would you call your next witness, please?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. Your Honour, we call Mr. Osmanovic. MR. IBRO OSMANOVIC, called.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: We were just thinking -- here is the witness. We can talk later after the witness. It is another matter that has nothing to do with this witness' testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Would you take the oath, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Would you please state your full name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My name is Osmanovic, Ibro.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was born on 5th August in 1965 at Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is Vlasenica located in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could retrieve Prosecution Exhibit 73, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sorry, but there is something wrong with what I can hear. I cannot hear it well. Some problems.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Can you hear in your language, Mr. Osmanovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I can now.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, would you look at Prosecution exhibit 73, the map? Would you take the pen or the pointer and point out to the court where Vlasenica is located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vlasenica is in north eastern Bosnia here.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If we could zoom on this section of the map for the court, please? Mr. Osmanovic, I note on the map an area marked Han Pijesak; would you point that out, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Han Pijesak is right next to Vlasenica, it borders Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is there a town of Han Pijesak as well as an Opstina of Han Pijesak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there is.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Is there a town of Vlasenica as well as an Opstina of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, could you tell us how long you have lived in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I lived there since I was born there, up until the day when I was arrested.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you know, what is the ethnic composition of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were 67 per cent Muslims and the rest were Serbs. In the Opstina, 63 per cent Muslims and the rest were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say you were from Vlasenica, were you from the town of Vlasenica itself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was, and that was also the municipality of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How large is the town of Vlasenica or how large was the town of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Vlasenica had 6,000 to 7,000 people.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know many of those people who lived in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, some 70 per cent of people who used to live there permanently.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know the ethnic group of those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, what is your ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am a Muslim Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was your prior occupation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I used to work in the furniture factory, "Sipad".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was that located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The factory was in the industrial zone of the town.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you ever perform any military service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only the regular military service in the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did you perform that service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 8th April 1984 up until 1985.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did you perform that service?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in Niksic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where is that located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Niksic is in Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were your duties in the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in reconnaissance, a reconnaissance soldier.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time that you were in the JNA, did you become familiar with the JNA equipment, uniforms, weapons and markings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time you were in Niksic in Montenegro, did you become familiar with the dialect spoken in that area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the period of time 1990 and 1991, did you notice the establishment of political parties in your area of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What parties were formed in the Vlasenica area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The SDA party, predominantly Muslim, SDS, the Serbian and SDP, the Former Communists.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you participate in the elections in your area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I participated in the election as every citizen of the country.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who won, what party won in your area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The SDS won.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: As a result of their victory, what political positions did they obtain in the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The result of the victory was that they could appoint the leading men of the Opstina and the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you refer to the "SUP", what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This was the Secretariat for the Interior, that means the police.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were there any JNA military posts in or near Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the territory of the Opstina of Vlasenica, there were no JNA troops, rather, there were no garrisons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were there any garrisons close to Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next one was in Han Pijesak. That was the nearest garrison.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Han Pijesak is the area you pointed out earlier?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How far was Han Pijesak from the town of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 18 kilometres and a half.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: If you know, what military units were located there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: JNA garrison, all sorts of formations but mostly infantry.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like to direct your attention to August 1991 and ask you if at that time you recall an incident that occurred in a church at Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Before the witness responds, we will stand in recess for 20 minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, before the recess, I had asked you if you recalled an incident that occurred in a church in Han Pijesak in August of 1991; do you recall such an incident?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Can you tell me were you present at this church at Han Pijesak when this incident occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was present. That was in front of the church.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A group of Reserves from Vlasenica billeted in Han Pijesak, they asked that group in attempt to sing the Serbian national songs celebrating the Serb Chetnik leaders of World War II.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say members of the Reserves, are you talking about the JNA reserves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of songs did they ask to be sung?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb nationalist songs forbidden in the former system in SFRY.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you remember what any of the lyrics of those songs were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I will not ask you to sing them, but could you tell us what the lyrics are that you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: "From Topola to Ravna Gora, all guys are of General Draza".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Any additional lyrics that you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One of the songs was this "From Topola to Ravna Gora"; another one is "Oh, Duke Sindjelic, you can hear the trumpet down to Kosovo".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise the names of any of these people that were included in the lyrics?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Well, when we learned history, those individuals were members of the Chetnik movement during World War II.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the meaning of those lyrics to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Derogatory, belittling meaning for Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the reaction of the people in front of the church when this request was made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of the people present there, some Muslims, simply left the celebration in protest.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These individuals who made this request, what were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were wearing regular uniforms of the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were those uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Grey, olive green. They had three parts; they had the shirt, the trousers and the jacket.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When they first made this request, were those songs played?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At that time is when Muslims began to leave that church area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In 1991, did you become aware of any mobilization of men in the Vlasenica area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you become aware of this mobilization?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was present, I was in Dragisa, Milakovic, when an officer of the JNA came and brought the summons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was Mr. Milakovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Milakovic was a man I saw every day; he was a friend of mine. Before the war we saw each other every day.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you know his ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he have any affiliation with the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war he spent a lot of time in uniform. He spent some time in Banja Luka and then in Han Pijesak and then in Milici in the garrison there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was he a member either of the active duty or the Reserve component of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Initially, he was in education, he was a Reserve.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: He was a Reserve, Reserve JNA member?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You said that a JNA officer came to him and brought him something. This JNA officer, what rank, insignia, did he wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was wearing the uniform of the JNA with regular ranks, insignia, of a Lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know this man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was it that he brought to Mr. Milakovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He brought him a large envelope and in this envelope were summonses.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity to actually see these summons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because I helped Milakovic to sort them out.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of the names on these summonses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The individuals whose names you recognised, did you know their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. They were of the Serb ethnic origin.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any Muslim names on these summons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were none.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the summons for, what did they say, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was saying summons to serve in the armed forces of the SFRY.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did Mr. Milakovic make any comment to you about these summonses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only that they were going to Banja Luka for a drill.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After seeing these summonses at Mr. Milakovic's house, after that time, did you begin to see more men in military uniforms in Serb parts of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the same time frame -- we are looking at the end of 1991 -- did you become aware of the creation of any new military units or locations in the Vlasenica area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A garrison at Milici was established.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you become aware of that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was present with Mr. Milakovic when he went to the garrison.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Milici, is that a village within the Opstina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is a mining settlement in the territory of the municipality of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What ethnic group or groups inhabit this area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They are almost all Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At the end of 1991 and into the spring of 1992, did you become aware of the creation of any Serb autonomous region in the Vlasenica area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the Serb autonomous region of Birac.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were there any Opstinas within this Serb autonomous region?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was Opstina Sekovici, Vlasenica, Bratunac, Srebrenica, Zvornik and the newly established Serb Opstina, Milici.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When the Serb autonomous region was formed, to your knowledge, were separate Serb Opstinas formed at the same time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Negotiations were on their way to set up Serb Opstinas in the territory of those.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was involved in those negotiations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The Serb Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did anyone ever tell you why the Serbs wanted to form these Serb autonomous regions and Serb Opstinas?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After the creation of this Serb autonomous region, did you yourself notice any increase in the number of men carrying weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it was not as many first before the war broke out.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After the war broke out, did you notice such an increase?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a large number, a large part, of the Serb population began to carry weapons around the town.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately when you first became aware of the creation of this Serb autonomous region in the Vlasenica area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This town was divided.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The town of Vlasenica was divided?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Serb Opstina -- Serb Vlasenica Opstina was set up.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the eve of the outbreak of the war.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 22nd April '92.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Prior to that, in the spring of 1992, did you notice any changes in your ability to get certain television stations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Media, of the media systems, only Belgrade television and Novi Sad television operated.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall when that occurred?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some time in the early days of the war in Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Do you recall what time frame that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 6th April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So this was prior to the conflict in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You indicated that the conflict in Vlasenica began on 22nd April. On that date, what did you observe happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All vital functions of the town were blocked, the town hall, bank, post office, police, the court, very many uniformed men people we did not know and local Serb population under arms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say that these institutions were blocked, they were blocked by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were blocked by the Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What uniforms did these soldiers wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: SMB, regular JNA uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you first become aware that the military had moved into the town of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 22nd April, in the morning hours, a police vehicle with a loud speaker was requesting that armaments, that weapons, legally obtained were to be surrendered, that the army was there to protect the people and that force would be used against those who did not obey.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see the individuals who were in this car from which this broadcast was being made?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only they were in uniforms; we could not recognise their faces.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On this date, on 22nd April, did you see any type of heavy weapons or armoured vehicles in the town of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, by the town stadium there were APCs and in the Muslim cemetery, they were also there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise these vehicles as being of the type that the JNA had?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When they said that people were to turn in their weapons, did they give any time by which this was to be done?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The ultimatum was until 9 o'clock.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You yourself that day, did you see any persons turning in weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of weapons were being turned in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were turning in their personal weapons, that is, pistols, revolvers and hunting weaponry.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of these people who were turning in weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The ones that you recognised, do you know what their ethnic group was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After this deadline for turning in weapons, this 9 p.m. deadline, after that time, did you see civilians with weapons in the town of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A local part of the Serb population in uniforms carried weapons, and some of these Serb local population wore white bands and also weapons.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During this day, this first day of 22nd April, did you have occasion to speak with any of the soldiers who had come into your town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first day in the afternoon of the first day, I talked to a soldier who originally came from Bijelo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where is that located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Bijelo Polje in Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How do you know that he came from Montenegro?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His pronunciation, that area is characteristic of a particular pronunciation. I recognised that and I asked him where he came from. He did not try to hide it. He said he came from Bijelo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he tell you what unit he was with?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He said he was serving in Sremska Mitrovica and that he was doing his regular military service.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Had you heard of the Sremska Mitrovica military unit before that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where is Sremska Mitrovica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sremska Mitrovica is in Srem on the Sava River; it belongs to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did he tell you what his name was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Predrag.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did Predrag ever tell you why he was in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, to calm down this possible conflict between the Muslims and the Serbs, possible conflicts.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Prior to that time, had there been any attacks by Muslims against Serbs, to your knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where was it that you saw this man?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Panorama Hotel.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see any other individuals in the hotel?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but I did not know some of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The ones that you did know, who were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were largely from the Secretariat of the Interior and the Serb Democratic Party.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On this day, on 22nd April, were any other orders given by these military people who had come into the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the movement was prohibited at night time, that is, the factories did not work.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Any other orders?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were the chief ones, to prevent movement during night time, that is, from the twilight to dawn.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you yourself go out after that curfew on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the curfew Dragisa Milakovic came to see me.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did he want to talk with you about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He showed me a few sheets of paper and told me to look at them. On one of them was my name, and he told me to take care of myself; that all sorts of fools were carrying weapons around these days.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there a number next to your name on that list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was that number?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see any of the other names on the list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise any of those names?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the part which I saw I recognised many names.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The names that you recognised, what was the ethnic group of those people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After he left and after the curfew, did you hear any sound of vehicular movement in your area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, vehicles patrolled the street.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During this day of 22nd April, were any of the businesses in Vlasenica open?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the following days, did some of the businesses in Vlasenica reopen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next day, Serb restaurants, pubs and shops were open or, rather, enterprises that belonged to the state were under the directions of labour.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see any Muslim businesses that you knew reopen in the following days?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After the military came in to Vlasenica, what changes, if any, did you notice in the living conditions in the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The changes that took place in the town and the conditions were the curfew which disrupted the structure of work or, rather, the fact that some people had reported to the Public Security Station the prohibition to leave the town.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you become aware of any new Serb departments or agencies being created?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry. After the military came into Vlasenica, did you become aware of any new Serb agencies or public divisions, departments, being created?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Serb municipalities, Opstina Serb Opstina, Vlasenica, with the seat in Vlasenica was set up.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What about the Fire Department, what happened with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That part of the Fire Brigade to which I belonged for many years, the structure changed. Muslims were now out of the question, and only three Serbs remained who were there before.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The police Station in Vlasenica, what happened with that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims were not working in the police Station there, and they were Serbs only.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you given any type of work obligation during this time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was that work obligation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I had to come to work, to the factory I worked in and to spend there working hours from 7.00 to 3.00.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you actually engage in performing duties there during those hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were those the same duties that you had performed before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The same thing that I did before only with a much lower intensity.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you paid for the performance of these duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the salary per diems nominally, but we never collected that money.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were there any restrictions as far as the amount of money that you could withdraw from the bank in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was limited to 5,000, that is, 5 billion Dinars, and that is 10,000 and 10 billion, which is about 70 German Marks.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you observe other individuals going into the bank and being able to withdraw much larger sums?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was present when a fellow worker filled in a cheque to a much larger sum than that, a much larger amount than that limit.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: The worker's ethnic group was what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During this time period, did you notice any type of graffiti on buildings in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On the houses of eminent Muslims there were graffiti such as "Ustasha", "Muslims out", "We will slaughter", "Out", "This is Serb, this is Serbia".

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did "Ustasha", that term, mean to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was another deprecating, belittling name because none of my family belonged to that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To what group did Ustasha refer, if you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Croat and Muslim groups.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After that first day that you saw Predrag at the Panorama Hotel, did you see him again in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I would like to direct your attention about the 22nd May and ask you what happened on that date.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 22nd May '92, I was detained in the police Station in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: On 22nd May 1992, did there remain military personnel in the city of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the town of Vlasenica there were members of the so-called Serb militia and Serb army.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During this time period from 22nd April to when the military initially entered on 22nd May, to your knowledge, had there been any type of armed resistance to this take over of Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During this time period from 22nd April until 22nd May, did you see any local inhabitants being sent from the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which local population? The Muslim local population had begun to leave the town; whereas the Serb local population remained in the town.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there any type of round up of people, of Muslim people, in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not yet.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The gathering up of Muslim population started somewhere around 18th May when the case of Sakopaca(?) happened, when the people started to go towards Tuzla in great numbers.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you say the case of Sakopaca began to happen, what are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The rumour had it that to Vlasenica that the Sakopaca village had been destroyed, physically destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At that point in time Muslim people began to leave Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did they leave, what type of transport?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those people who had a personal vehicle used that vehicle; those people who did not have a vehicle, a bus was organised, starting from the bus station in Vlasenica that took the people out.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you able to leave the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I was forbidden to do that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you were arrested, who was it who arrested you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Members of the so-called Serb militia, Bastah Dragan and Zoran Djuric and then also Rade Milic and a person whom I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was this Serb militia that you referred to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The unit, and it was written "Serb militia", that means the Reserve, the Reserve Serbian policemen of the police Station in Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These men that you named, their ethnic group was all Serb?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of uniform did they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Dragan Bastah was wearing a camouflage uniform; the others wore the uniform of war police.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is that uniform?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The uniform is dark blue.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you taken after you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: I wonder if it would be possible to have "war police" explained? Does it mean the same thing as military police?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour. (To the witness): Mr. Osmanovic, when you referred to "war police", what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the previous system of the Yugoslav state, there was the active duty policemen and the Reserve police. The Reserve police were activated in case of war, and they were different only in their uniform; one wore light blue and the other dark blue uniforms, but their arms and insignia were the same.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These war police that you refer to, are these civilian police or military police?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilian.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did they take you once they arrested you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the police Station.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: At the police Station in Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened once you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was imprisoned without any explanation.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was held there until 2nd June.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were other people held there with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were there, were you physically abused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Personally, yes, and other people as well.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was done to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was beaten. In that police Station I was interrogated for some alleged cannon I never saw.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who was it that administered these beatings to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zoran Obrenovic; he was the one who beat most among others called Viskovic, Garic and Vukavic(?)

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Those people you have just named, who are they, are they persons who beat others or are they victims who were beaten?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These were people who were beating other people.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were of Serb nationality.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of uniform did they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Obrenovic, Garic and Viskovic wore camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many times did these beatings occur while you were being held here at the police Station?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Sometimes twice, sometimes once, and they were very lucky days when they did not happen at all.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What injuries did you sustain as a result of those beatings?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those beatings, I had five broken teeth and part of my leg and then on both of my hands I have marks from a knife.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: When you were taken from the police Station, where were you taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 2nd June, I was transferred to the municipality prison of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Until 18th June.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were you transported there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was transported on foot. I was taken on foot to the prison.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who took you there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken by Miljanic(?), the policeman.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now while you were at the Opstina prison, were you mistreated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the nature of that mistreatment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly beatings, thirst, we were hungry. We were not allowed to sleep. I had to loot Muslim property for them. We had to do the dirtiest types of duties in town and then bury the dead.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You say that while you were at the prison you had to take Muslim property. Where was this property located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To take valuable objects from Muslim houses and we had to put them in a large warehouse that was near the municipal prison.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now when you were taken out to loot these houses, who would take you to do this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly they would come in camouflage uniforms; those were younger men, all of them from Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did they wear any type of insignia or patches on their uniforms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Neither insignia nor emblems.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You say that you knew most of them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb nationality.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: You also indicated that at one point you had to bury dead bodies?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where did this occur?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The room settlement, some 3 kilometres from Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who took you there to perform these duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken by Ljubisa Vukotic and Zoran Obrenovic and Sladjan Pajic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were you transported there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken there by a tractor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now this village of Drum, to your knowledge what was the ethnic composition of that village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were only two houses that were Serb; all the other houses were Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many bodies did you have to bury that day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Twenty-two.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These bodies, what type of clothing were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the gender of these people?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry, what was the gender of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were males; they were all men.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was their age group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 18 to 65 years old.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Four of them I knew.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you see any type of wounds or injuries on them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hodic had bullets all over his chest, and all the others had a bullet in their front.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: "In their front", you mean the front part of their body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of the head, above their eyes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now how did you bury them? What did you use?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Already a hole that had been dug out by a machine of the company, and we just had to put them there and then take all the valuables out of their pockets and the machine put everything on them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How many people in addition to yourself were chosen to perform this duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three others.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know these three?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have to perform any other duties while you were held at the Opstina prison?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we had to dig the rows on the front line between Vlasenica and Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And how were you taken there to perform this duty?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Truck, a military truck.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you recognise the truck as a JNA type vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The model was TAM 110.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who took you there to dig these trenches or row at the front line?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: People in the uniforms, in grey, olive grey uniforms, SMB.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just two of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And the ones that you knew, where were they from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were from the village of Misari, a Serb village.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long did you remain at the front lines digging these rows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We went there twice a day; in the morning and then we would come back in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was there any fighting going on in this area while you were digging these rows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I believe you indicated you were held at the prison until the 18th June?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where were you taken on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 18th June I was transferred to the camp of Susica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And how you were taken there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Truck that belonged to Dragan Bastah.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Was this a civilian type vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were you taken there by yourself or were other persons transferred as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A group from the prison and a group from the police station.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have any escorts when you were taken to Susica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were in prison. There was a canvas and the people who accompanied us were behind.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were these people wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: I am sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: police uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
