utterances.text: Did you know any of these people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the company that accompanied us there was the police with a police car and the people who were with us they were all wearing civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now where is Susica to which you were taken?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Susica is by the main road to from Sarajevo to Belgrade that goes through the region of Rumania towards Han Pijesak.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So it was in the Han Pijesak area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that was in the area of the municipality of Vlasenica.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you held at Susica camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Till 30th June.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now, while you were at Susica camp did you see any guards around the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did these guards wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They wore uniforms, standard JNA uniforms, and standard weapons, normal weapons in the JNA.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of these guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Most of them.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And where were they from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were from Vlasenica and the nearby villages.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Serbs.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were held at Susica were there other detainees being held there as well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, 550 people.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you know any of these other detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The people who came from the area of the Vlasenica municipality.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Those you knew, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now during your time at Susica did you learn who was in charge of the camp there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The commander was Dragon Nikolic called Jenki.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How did you know that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He arrived to the camp, he said that he was the commander of the camp, the god, the law and without his permission nobody could go out of the camp.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did he wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He wore a camouflage uniform and a cap on his head with a Kokarda. He wore two grenades on his belt, a knife, a pistol and he always had an automatic rifle of the 767 calibre.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now when you say he wore a Kokarda, could you explain for us, could you describe that for us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the symbol of the Chetniks from the Second World War. It contains a two headed eagle, a skull, and bones that cross on it.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Susica, what were the living conditions like? What was the food like that you received?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We received one meal per day.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And how much food did you receive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just as much to survive.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of food did you receive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Rice and bread. A piece of bread, one piece of bread, one loaf of bread for 12 people.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What were your living and sleeping conditions like in this camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We slept on the concrete. Some people had a jacket and they would sleep on the jacket. We were not able to wash or bath; no kind of personal hygiene because we had no conditions, no possibility to do that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These other detainees who were held at Susica, what was their gender?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Apart from seven women all the rest were men.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was the age group of the detainees held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From 10 to 80 years old.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Susica camp, were you physically abused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Physically abused once by Dragon Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And while you were at Susica camp did you see other detainees there being abused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: By whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mostly by Dragon Nikolic and after that Ljuibisa Vukotic came and Zoran Obrenovic, Sladjan Pajic, Goran Pajic, Goran Viskovic called "Vjetar", the wind.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: All of these people who came to the camp, were they allowed free access to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were always accompanied by Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These other detainees that you saw abused, what did you see done to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some people were only beaten, physically mistreated, beaten, and to other people they injured them by pistol, rifle butts on their head or the knives. They killed four people. They beat two people to death.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These four people that they killed, did you see these people's bodies after they were dead?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Then why do you say that they killed four people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Because the guys that were with us they had to bury them in the morning and myself, I was woken up that evening by Zoran Obrenovic and Sladjan Pajic. They took three persons out, Dzevad Saric, Muso Zekic and Muharem Kolerovic. I was taken to the door and then Ljuban Kuduric took me back, and instead of me a fourth person was taken out. We heard the rifle, one shot, and that was it. In the morning the brothers Ferhatovic went to bury them and when they came back they told us that they buried those four people.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These four people, if you know, what was their ethnic group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Susica camp, were there any official visitors to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, twice.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And these official visitors, did you learn who they were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: One had the insignia of a major, of a JNA major, and he told us that we will be exchanged. On one occasion Nikolic made us go out and then collect all the papers and clean everything around because the commander was coming, the king.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After he said this, can you describe the person who arrived at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A man came with a civilian vehicle, the make was Golf, and he had a lieutenant insignia, wearing a camouflage uniform with heavily guarded.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you learn his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We knew that his name was Kraljevic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And did Dragon Nikolic tell you what this man's position was or where he came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. No, he did not tell us where he came from, but while we were clearing everything he said, "Yes, Kraljevic is coming, the commander is coming."

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened when this lieutenant arrived at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Nothing. He arrived and they sat in a building where usually guards used to be and then he left.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now you said that at one point a JNA major came to the camp to talk about an exchange. Do you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He came I think 24th on 25th June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now were you at that time exchanged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, people were transported on 27th.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now were you yourself taken to another camp after Susica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 13th June I was transferred to the camp of Batkovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where is that camp located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Batkovic is some 12 kilometres from Bijelina towards the Sava.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were you taken to Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were transferred by bus and were heavily guarded.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What type of bus was this, military or civilian?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Civilian bus.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now these guards who went with you on the bus, were they guards from Susica camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. They came specially to accompany us.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Had you ever seen them before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Just one of them, Shakovic.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where had you seen Shakovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shakovici.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Where is that located?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some 20 kilometres from Vlasenica in the direction of Kalesija, that is Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: It is a village, this Shakovici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. This is a small town that was the centre of the Opstina of Shakovici.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: To your knowledge what ethnic group lived there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Serb nationality.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These escorts that took to you Batkovic, what did they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They wore JNA uniforms, armed. They had regular JNA weapons and the vehicles had the JNA plates.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were other individuals taken with you to Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How long were you held at Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: June 1992 till the 21st July 1993.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now the guards at the Batkovic camp, what types of uniforms did they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: SMB uniforms, except for one everybody called him Veljko.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What was his position at the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He used to come there every day, opened the doors, call out people. He would permit some people to go to work; he would be there when new people would be coming.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time that you were at Batkovic, were there other detainees held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I arrived in the camp of Batkovic were all the people who were, all the people that left Vlasenica before.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Batkovic were you yourself mistreated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The abuse started the from the moment we arrived.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What happened when you arrived?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On our arrival they made us run the gauntlet. We each and every one of us had to run it. They would beat us up until to the door, and then they would call a row and we had to go one by one to the corner of the hangar. Then they called the row once again, according to the list, and then we had to run the same type of gauntlet and then line up by the wall.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These people between whom you were running, the people who were beating you, what were they wearing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They wore SMB uniforms camouflage uniforms. They were dressed in a different way but nobody wore civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you come to learn who any of these people were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were they camp employees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some of them stayed there as guards, as sentries in the camp and they were wearing SMB uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time that you were held at Batkovic you indicated the abuse began when you arrived. Did the abuse continue during the time you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the time that you were there did you ever see other detainees abused?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, regularly.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did you see done to them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were beaten until they lost consciousness and one of them was battered to death.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And who did the battering?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Damorvic was beaten by all of the guards present there.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And the others who were beaten, who beat them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All of them. They all took pleasure in that.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: While you were at Batkovic did you ever have to perform duties outside the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Outside the camp we went to the Muslim village of Kora and Oglena and we felled trees, we dug trenches at the front line. We did everything from agricultural, from farming work and onward.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now when you were taken to the front line to dig these trenches, how were you transported there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were transported there in trucks.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What types of trucks?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The trucks sent by the JNA Deitz.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What is "Deitz"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Deitz is a truck manufactured by the truck company in Maribor.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And did you have escorts when you were taken to the frontlines?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Who escorted you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Usually armoured guards.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What did they wear?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: SMB uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: These duties at the frontline, to your knowledge were any of the people with you ever injured or killed while performing these duties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ahmed Basic, he was born in the village of Dilitinja , Zvornik on 5th December 1992, and Ferhudin from the municipality of Kalesija on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: How were they injured or killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A shell fell and Ferhudin received six wounds and Basic died in the hospital. He was wounded in the stomach.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Now you indicated that in July 1993 you left Batkovic. How were you allowed to leave on that date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The International Committee of the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: So you were part of an exchange?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, prior to the soldiers coming in and taking over Vlasenica, were you part of any Muslim armed force or organised resistance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you resist the takeover of your town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Did you have any weapons to turn over when your town was taken over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: After 22nd April and before your arrest, did you become part of any Muslim armed force or armed resistance unit?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: During the April takeover of Vlasenica did you see any signs of armed resistance to that take over?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: You have referred to, particularly at Batkovic, men in SMB uniforms. Were some of them sometimes wearing hats or caps?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: With the exception of the escort which arrived with us from Vlasenica, they were wearing camouflage, white brimmed hats and all the others were bare headed.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Were they wearing on their uniforms, the SMB uniforms, emblems of any sort, any emblems or identifying signs?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the beginning, no, except for individuals, some individuals wore badges or Kokardas, but only individuals and most of them simply wore JNA uniforms.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE STEPHEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, you mentioned that you were made to loot Muslim property. Was this removal done from one or two Muslim properties or was it done from several?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Several Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, how many persons approximately were detained at the Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the Batkovic camp there were close to 3,000 of us. The people came and left and then new ones came. The first group that came to Batkovic was from Kalesija; the second from Vlasenica; the third from Koraj; the fourth from Zvornik; the fifth from Zavicia; the sixth from Ugljevik; the seventh from Brcko; the eighth from Brezevo Polje; the ninth from Telnova; the tenth from Bosanski Samac, Sanski Most and Mijacia.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Are all of these towns in Bosnia-Herzegovina, the towns you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: And what ethnic groups did these persons belong to, the detainees?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first groups that arrived were Muslims and then Croats were also with us.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: In this Susica camp you said there were 550 people held there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: What ethnic group did they belong to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: Just Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only Muslims.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Miss Hollis, do you have any additional questions in the light of my questions?

utterances.speaker: MISS HOLLIS
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Any questions, Mr. Wladimiroff?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Very good. Is there any objection to Mr. Osmanovic being permanently excused?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Mr. Osmanovic, you are permanently excused. Thank you for coming. We would like to remain with counsel for a few moments to discuss a matter that we had raised yesterday, I guess it was. (The witness withdrew). The matter had to do with the possibility of counsel meeting to discuss ways to perhaps expedite the trial without in any way intruding on any one's desire to present the case as fully as he or she wishes. Where are we with that discussion? Mr. Wladimiroff, I think you had told me that your team was not going to be altogether complete over Thursday and Friday and Saturday and Sunday. Then you also had some question as to whether you wanted to participate in such a meeting. So I suppose I will turn to you first.

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: We have given it very brief thought so far. I think Mr. Orie and myself will contact the Prosecution office to see whether we can meet on Friday, and just sit and listen to what the Prosecution may come up with and we will just do that.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Niemann, do you have anything to report at this time?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: No, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: So then you will make the time arrangements I gather with Mr. Wladimiroff and Mr. Orie to discuss perhaps what can be done with respect to the offering of evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, we will contact the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE PRESIDING JUDGE
utterances.text: OK, very good. We will stand adjourned until Monday at 10 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: (The hearing adjourned for a short time)
(The court adjourned for a short time)
